The first 90% of the game is great, but the final area is very tedious.

Spoilers:
[spoiler]The final area has several different bosses that you have to find and kill. Each boss has strengths and weaknesses that require specific gear, but you don't know which boss is which until you aggro them, and then you have to kite them while fumbling with the inventory system to equip the correct gear. You also can't move with your inventory open, so you're almost guaranteed to die at least once at each boss. Also, the final area has a damage over time effect that must be mitigated by using specific gear and medicine (the boss areas don't require this gear), and you'll need to have multiple sets of that gear due to the fact that you have to die and retrieve your gear at least once for each boss[/spoiler]
It's good to have an ending in a Tarkov-like game, make all the exploring and collecting actually meaningful.

I was trying to figure out why this game felt so familiar, even though I've never played a true extraction shooter. And then it hit me...

This game is Dredge.

Yes, you heard that right, now hear me out. Sure it's ducky and tarkov-y (at least from what I've heard), but it is also Dredge-y. At least earlier on in the game.

In Dredge, you take your little dinghy boat out into a monstrous unknown world each day to loot and loot and pray you don't die. In Duckov, you take your cute little ducky duck out into a scary new frontier to shoot and loot and pray you make it back home before dark. It's the same gameplay loop and I love it.

Dredge is my only perfect game on Steam so far, but Duckov very well might be my second.

Thank you Dredgkov.

I've literally got nothing bad to say about this game. 

It's EXTREMELY FUN. Extremely optional with how casual you want it to be. 
The ONLY things I could even nitpick would simply be mistranslations and some missing UI stats and that's it.

The gameplay loop is solid, the quest direction is great, and mechanically the game just works. 
You'll get frustrated at times when not able to locate certain drops, but that comes with the territory of these types of looter shooters. There are hidden merchants who sell the items as well if you're keen enough to locate them. 

Tons of mods, unfortunately all of them are in Chinese and tough to figure out what they do, but there are some great ones.

DEFINITELY WORTH THE PURCHASE. I have yet to even complete the game yet at 126 hours, though I've just now unlocked the ability to trigger Game Ending #0.

Fun game if you've always liked the thought of looter/extractor shooter as a single player game (3rd person top down not 1st person). Early to mid game is fantastic! Gun play and survival mechanics scratch a certain itch. Beating even a low level NPC when you're against the ropes is highly rewarding. The end game though sucks big ole beach balls. End game needs to be balanced desperately!

"What's Wrong With the End Game" you asked?
All your best gear is rendered useless in exchange for a Storm Suit (Hazmat Suit) that has no protection and mediocre elemental weapons (not as good as they sound). The toughest enemies (hp, defense, damage, fire rate, movement - all top notch) just absolutely swarm you.

Aggravating Notes:
1. Any time you do a corpse run you must get your corpse/gear in one run (you may not return to base and try a second time to get your corpse/gear).
2. You must have certain equipment pieces to proceed through certain areas (gas mask, thermal goggles, Storm Suit). In my experience it is not stated anywhere prior to venturing into a new area that new equipment is needed. Like the power room of J-lab B2 (Good luck getting new thermal goggles in one run at that point).
3. Enemies spawn in with different ammo constantly. You can not prepare to go against certain enemies because one run they may have AP ammo lvl 3 then the next they have incendiary ammo.
4. Now here's the kicker... there is an in-game feature that allows you reload a previous save file therefore gaining any items lost (timing of save file matters too obviously). However it kills any sense of completion because death becomes like any other game. So you're stuck with wasting time building back up or just reloading.

For me to give a thumbs up there would have too be a guaranteed way to reclaim lost items that are necessary to progress through certain areas. Example: always have a red key card and thermal goggles spawn separately in certain areas within J-lab that give players a chance to reclaim their corpse/gear. Or even make players aware that the final Storm Area you go to requires both the suit and injectors to survive with an early unlock for the better suit.

Don't let the silly presentation fool you into thinking this is a joke game. It's a genuinely good single player extraction shooter. It's not perfect, but it's really good overall.

The good:
- A proper single player extraction shooter. Which means, no jank from mods like Single Player Tarkov (SPT is fantastic, but it is kinda janky), being able to pause the game etc. The game also creates save backups so if you want to roll back your save after bugs or whatnot, you can. Nice!
- Fairly good new player experience. The game explains mechanics a fair bit, and introduces you to them one by one in a tutorial area
- Several difficulty settings, including choosing between losing all your gear when you die, or being able to go back in and loot your body
- Generally, while it is still a difficult game, it is not nearly as punishing as (singleplayer) Tarkov. Personally, i think it's a good balance
- Clearly strongly inspired by Tarkov not just in name, you will recognize a lot of enemies, map areas, hideout structures, items like GPUs and LEDXs and more, which can be pretty fun. But Duckov is not a straight copy, it also does it's own thing and puts a spin on things
- In particular, progress is reasonably fast paced
- You can Improve certain character stats by unlocking upgrades that cost resources, instead of leveling skills by using them, which works much better
- Customize your build with picking a talent, or equipping totems, to fit your playstyle
- The game tells you when you need certain items for hideout structures, or quests. Awesome!
- Obviously doesn't take itself too seriously, in a good way. Quests can be pretty funny
- Absurd customization options for your character
- It is overall (but not always) relatively easy to figure out where you need to go and what you need to do, you do not need a wiki to play it like Tarkov.
- Very cheap, while offering a ton of content. 18€ at the time of writing, and i played 30h and i am not nearly done yet
- Mod support!

The bad:
- Inventory management is a nightmare. The misc category could REALLY use to be split into several sub-categories, when a single category becomes 10-15 pages it takes ages to find anything specific. Organizing totems in particular are just terrible, you can't even see their name properly and have to mouse over them. Controls are also too simplified arguably, for most actions you just press "F" which can lead to doing the wrong thing when you're not super careful, you can also not quickly transfer keys from a key case in the stash for example. It's probably one of the biggest issues with the game, because you need to constantly interact with this system
- Without mods, even if you play on normal you can only loot ONE set of gear you lost. So if you die multiple times, sucks to be you - in a singleplayer game with adjustable difficulty, this really should not be the case
- Generally, i immediately installed a bunch of mods. It's nice to have mod support, but please include more basic features in the base game to begin with, like range indicators for the crosshair, or how many of an item you have on you and in storage, or looting your gear for multiple deaths
- Some quests can be...awful. Looking at you Vidas M700 kill quest
- Also, the number of times you get a quest asking you to literally do something you just did...please just be a bit smarter. For example, i literally found the Lab location on my own and after extracting got the quest to go there to explore it after having completed a different quest. Like, seriously? It just really takes you out of it. Or quest to kill a certain boss literally after i just killed them in the last raid. It would totally be possible to track those things, and acknowledge you did them when you get the quest, which would make it into a great moment instead of a frustrating one
- Too many quests that ask you to kill enemies with a certain gun. Especially bad when it asks for Stg 77 and the Stg 77A3 variant does NOT count!
- Hitboxes of environment are frustrating. You often cannot shoot over something you think you should, or can when you think you shouldn't (more accurately, enemies will shoot you when you think they shouldn't). Similarly enemies will often shoot at you when they cannot see you at all, like you being behind a wall but they laser onto you already. Or they can hit you at a corner when you can't even see them
- While it's not as bad as Tarkov, it would be nice to have bit more direction at times
- Mix of real and fudged names for weapons. Purely one or the other would feel nicer than a mix
- While overall drop rates seem not as grindy as Tarkov, they can still be annoying at times and lock progress behind hours and hours of farming thanks to RNG
- Generally the pacing can be a bit inconsistent. At first you will unlock a ton of personal upgrades, but then at some point i was suddenly stuck behind a specific item i just couldn't get yet for a long time
- I'm not a huge fan of how injectors work. You can't use them while stored in an injector case, and their effects can also be rather short

Duckov is not perfect, but it's probably the best singleplayer extraction shooter out there right now. The mod support also means some issues that the base game has can be improved.
If the idea interests you at all, highly recommend giving it a go, especially with how cheap it is!

Having 100%'d the game now, in 170 hours, I definitely recommend it, but a few things in the game are a MASSIVE grind for little reward, and the mid-to-end game gets pretty tedious and slow.

Starting the game, there are loads of quests to complete, limited resources that require careful management, and plenty of locations to explore. Once you've completed the first 50-75% of the quests, however, finishing the rest becomes pretty dry, and many of them require RNG drops that seem to have a 1% or less drop rate. Getting the third game for the console, as well as the J-Lab purple and yellow cards, for example, took literally dozens of trips to their respective drop sites before they finally showed up, and the game doesn't give you much to do while you wait for that to happen.

Secondly, all of the vendor supplies and upgrades are on timers, and some of them are VERY long. It takes many hours to acquire the resources needed to unlock the various character and warehouse upgrades, and when you finally have what you need, you click "start research" and it starts a real-time timer of up to 2 hours. Crafting items, ammunition for example (which obviously you need a lot of), requires items that are found while exploring the maps, which takes a great deal of time, as well as items purchasable in shops at base. Once you have spent all the time needed to find enough resources to craft ammunition, you have to buy additional resources at the shops, but there are only 10 of each available every 2-5 minutes (depending on the shop). So, in order to craft a full stack of shotgun shells, for example (100), I have to buy 10 gun powders, then wait 2 minutes, then buy 10 more, and wait 2 minutes, over and over until I have enough to make 100 shells. This whole process is an arbitrary time sink that just feels awful.

Lastly, the final set of character upgrades (from the Street Vendor in the Warehouse Area) require a total of 3,100 "Blue Cubes" which are picked up in J-Lab at 75-150 per visit (they appear randomly in boxes that are always in the same locations, but also may or may not spawn), so the end game is basically going to J-Lab (or the storm area, in the most recent update) and searching the same 8-12 boxes over and over and over again until you have amassed enough Blue Cubes to finish out all the upgrades. Here again there's not much else to do while you're doing this, and it's also one of the last things you do in the game, so the upgrades aren't even really necessary anyway. If that requirement of 3,100 blue cubes was cut to 310, it'd still be tedious to collect them all, but you might have it done while those upgrades still have value rather than after completing the game.

All that said, I did grind it out (with a massive spreadsheet on my second monitor, tracking my progress and items), and doing so was great fun. I started over on a higher difficulty, because I didn't want to be done with the game once I had finished it, but I definitely won't be 100% finishing my second playthrough. It'll just be nice to play again knowing what to hold onto, and how much, what I can safely sell for money, which upgrades to go for and when, which weapons to keep and use, etc, because the game isn't really clear on any of that from the start.

This is an absolute gem of a game. It has a ton of looting to do, some intense moments, time to chill back at base, lots of quests, and absolutely no microtransactions, ads, or toxic players to deal with. It's definitely not developed by the team that made that [i]other[/i] game with a similar name.

There's a bunch of workshop items to make the game better as well. I've found several gems there.

One downside is that you can go through a run with little to no chance to find what you're looking for, but that's the nature of random loot distribution. The game wouldn't be as much fun otherwise.
